title: Location attestation ledger + staged regional failover constraints for Private/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tamper-evident attestation ledger and a staged regional failover constraint for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Goals: 1) Provide customers cryptographically-signed evidence that their requests were served within declared geographic boundaries and retention windows; 2) Prevent automatic uncontrolled region failover for residency-constrained workloads by introducing staged evacuation policies, operator approvals, and gating of evacuation events; 3) Automate periodic audit bundle exports to customer-configured destinations and Redwood audit retention. The feature should integrate with KMS for signing, the existing private control plane for deployment policy enforcement, and Console for per-customer attestations and export logs.
acceptance_criteria: Attestations produced per deployment node that include deployment_id, node_id, locality (region/az), timestamp, retention_policy_id, and request-hash counts
Ledger stores SHA-256 hashes of signed attestations and persists daily digest to customer-configured S3 or internal archival bucket
Automated weekly audit bundles generated (signed, compressed) and uploaded to customer destination or made available via Console download

Failover policy configuration for Private deployments: (a) mode: disabled | staged | automatic; (b) staged requires operator approval and allows roll-forward to next region after cooldown; (c) evacuation gating based on capacity and customer allowance
Console shows per-deployment attestation history, last-signed-digest, and a QRable verification token for offline verification
End-to-end tests exercising nodal attestation, ledger append, signature verification, and bundle export succeed in CI
Security review completed and KMS signing keys rotated per policy; documentation published in Confluence
design_notes: We will implement node-local attestation agents that emit JSON-LD style attestations, sign them with a node-local private key protected by the customer-managed KMS/HSM where available or Redwood-managed KMS for hosted private installs. To avoid storing large blobs in the ledger, persist only the SHA-256 of each attestation with timestamp and signature metadata; full attestations are kept in an encrypted archival store for the configured retention window. For on-prem installs with strict air-gaps, provide an option to export signed attestations via an offline bundle. Failover behavior: introduce a staged evacuation actor that requires a configurable approval window (default 30m) and a pre-evacuation health check that verifies KV cache flush success and checkpointing of in-flight requests. For safety, allow a maximum concurrent evacuation rate per-customer to avoid mass cross-region movement during network partitions.
implementation_plan: Prototype attestation agent (node daemon) and proof-of-concept ledger using S3 + Dynamo-like index
Add KMS signing integration and key management flows (customer KMS + Redwood fallback)
Extend Private control plane API to accept residency policy and failover_mode fields
Console UI: Attestation history panel, manual evacuation workflow with approve/reject actions
Create periodic audit-bundle producer Lambda/worker with upload hooks (S3, GCS, HTTPS webhook)
E2E tests, load tests for ledger throughput, and chaos tests for staged evacuation behavior
Prepare runbook and operator playbook for manual failover + rollback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ledger throughput under high-volume workloads could cause disk/IO spikes. Mitigation: batch hash writes, use append-only segmented files, and rate-limit attestation emission per node.
Risk: Customers may require air-gapped export; Mitigation: support offline bundle generation and signed bundle verification tool that runs locally.
Risk: KMS integration increases attack surface; Mitigation: perform security review, require least-privilege roles, and rotate keys regularly.

Risk: Staged evacuation delays can increase exposure to degraded performance. Mitigation: expose strict SLA trade-offs and allow customer override for emergency auto-evacuation with explicit opt-in and logging.
testing_plan: Unit tests for attestation serialization and signature verification, integration tests for ledger append and digest generation, CI job that spins up a 3-node private cluster and simulates a staged evacuation, and manual pen-test of key management flows. Add observability: per-node attestation rate, failed-signature counts, bundle-export success rate.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gate per-customer. Start with internal Redwood staging org and two pilot customers (legal agreements signed). Monitor metrics for failed exports and evacuation latencies for 2 weeks, then gradually enable for more customers. Provide a migration tool to backfill attestations for existing nodes for up to 90 days where archival data exists.
